source.title: The Benefits of Over-parameterization at Initialization in Deep ReLU Networks

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies activation and gradient norms at initialization, not whether training reaches low classification error or whether initialization changes learning speed or trainable depth.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior work reporting that wider networks train faster, but does not test that result. Its own empirical results compare activation and gradient norm ratios at initialization; these are related to the claim's subject but do not measure a listed version.
record.test_reason: The study derives and measures activation and gradient norm preservation at initialization. It reports no training trajectories, learning speeds, training errors or trainable-depth comparisons. These initialization properties concern V4's proposed mechanism but do not test its learning outcomes.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors derive finite-width norm-preservation guarantees at He initialization and empirically check them. The backward-pass guarantee assumes uniform widths and an explicit independence assumption; the forward-pass results also address infinite input sets. They do not demonstrate faster learning or successful training at greater depth.
record.recipe_differences: The paper analyzes and empirically checks norm preservation at initialization; it does not run a training-error or learning-speed comparison.
record.method_sensitivity: Width improves the reported approximation under He initialization; gradient norm equality is more accurate when layer widths vary less.

fits_no_version.finding: At initialization, He-initialized ReLU networks approximately preserve activation and parameter-gradient norm ratios, with better approximation at greater widths. Gradient norm equality improves with more uniform layer widths. Glorot initialization lacks these properties in the tested networks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sufficiently wide deep ReLU networks have approximate activation and parameter-gradient norm equality at He initialization, with accuracy depending on width and width uniformity.

record.problems: The empirical results are presented in figures without exact values in the text. The experiments measure norms at initialization and do not report training outcomes.

untested.parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10/100, including corrupted labels and dependence on size or training recipe.
Spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons in two-layer teacher-student problems.
Training degradation with depth, identity shortcuts, and successful training of very deep plain or unnormalized residual networks.
Whether initialization changes learning speed or trainable depth; orthogonal versus Gaussian training comparisons; training very deep convolutional networks.
Training loss, curvature and divergence near or above learning-rate stability thresholds.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparable training using Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The cannot_determine states refer to the listed claim versions, not uncertainty about the qualitative norm results. Section 4.2 additionally checks bound tightness, but supplies no missing result bearing on a version.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100, random or corrupted labels, and the effects of size, training duration, early stopping, or regularization.
Spurious local minima in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and the effect of student width.
Training error across depth, identity shortcuts, and training very deep plain or unnormalized residual networks.
Learning speed and trainable depth under different initializations, including orthogonal versus Gaussian weights and very deep convolutional networks.
Loss and curvature behavior at learning rates above or near stability limits.
Whether batch normalization changes accuracy gain or learning-rate tolerance, and whether Fixup enables comparable residual-network training.

rows.subject: 10 layer deep ReLU network
rows.size_stated: widths {100, 500, 2000, 4060}; 2000 randomly generated input samples in R500 and target labels in R20
rows.operation_detail: Measured hidden activation norm divided by input norm at initialization under He initialization.
rows.measure: Mean ratio of hidden activation norm to input norm over the dataset
rows.uncertainty: Small standard deviation; exact values figure only.
rows.note: The text says the ratio is roughly 1 and the approximation improves with larger width; no exact plotted values are stated.
rows.check: The text reports a ratio roughly equal to 1, improving with width; the reference value is 1. This measures initialization norm preservation, not a listed version's training outcome.
